summary: Frontend editor smoke-tested on the public React preview: load, toolbar presence, markup drawing, prompts, undo/redo clicks, rotate/export, safe paste/capture cancellation, and mobile toolbar all executed.

integration_issues.flow: React markup followed by rotate/adjustment/image redraw
integration_issues.issue: Canvas edits are drawn directly on the canvas, while the image/brightness/contrast/filter/rotation effect redraws the source image. Any later redraw can erase previously merged markup; undo/redo only changes history labels and does not restore canvas pixels.

action_items: Persist canvas snapshots or a merged bitmap for every edit and make undo/redo restore pixels, not only history labels.
Ensure rotation, crop, resize, and adjustment redraws preserve existing annotations.
critical_code_review_comments: React App.js uses a source-image useEffect that redraws the entire canvas whenever image or adjustment state changes, but markup is not stored separately; this violates the requirement that edits merge into the final image.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Public React smoke flow passed. Re-test markup persistence across rotate/adjustment/crop/resize and verify pixel-level undo/redo. Standalone artifact was code-reviewed but not opened through a static server in this run.
rca of the issue: Annotations are painted imperatively onto canvas, but the React effect treats the canvas as a rendering target for the original image and reruns on image/adjustment/rotation changes. There is no bitmap snapshot stack, so history state cannot restore visual content.
